findings.text: Upheld as a defect (question 4, a dead path; question 9 would also apply). In levelRefusal, the `reason === "allowed" ? "level-local"` arm can never run. The arm runs only when the level is `local`. Every row in policy.levels is built by effectiveLevel (policy.ts:178), which returns `allowed` only with a level above local (levels.ts:62). levelOf's other two paths return `unknown-destination`, `no-project` or `level-local`. No test builds a local/allowed pair either: every `reason: "allowed"` under tests/ comes with level knowledge. The line is new in the diff (diff.patch:11055). The arm also turns a broken invariant into a plausible refusal, which hides its cause. Fix: return `reason` directly. If an invariant check is wanted, make it throw instead of quietly mapping the case.
Upheld as advisory. A doc comment with no declaration under it was left behind when counterOfEpoch moved to levels.ts (question 10).
Upheld as advisory. The DESTINATIONS doc comment sits above REMOTE_ALIAS, so DESTINATIONS at line 14 has no comment (questions 6 and 10). This is housekeeping and changes no behaviour.

Upheld as advisory, as the reviewer filed it. Nothing reads EffectiveShareList's fileList and ignored fields, and fileListsOf (src/sharing/store.ts:414) parses the env file's lists a second time (questions 2 and 8).
Upheld as advisory. Only a test imports the re-export of GENERATION_KEY and newGeneration, and REBIND is exported but used only in its own file (question 8: an unused export is advisory).
Upheld as advisory. policyWith is a test helper exported from a production module (question 8).
Upheld as advisory. The two sharing key names are declared again in patch.ts, share.ts, status/report.ts and Sharing.vue, beside settings.ts's SHARING_KEYS (question 2: duplicated boilerplate).
Upheld as advisory, as the reviewer filed it. listProjects repeats entryAliases' query and its isHostLedAlias filter (question 2).

Upheld as advisory. The optional RestoreOptions.dataDir falls back to resolvePaths().dataDir, a path only older tests use. The fallback hides no failure (question 9).

Upheld as advisory. AC-5's recorded text in criteria-round-four.md says 'with a sent record of another version, send'. The test asserts keep/already-sent for the same hash at any version. That matches the spec line in force (spec.md:333), and spec.md:346 records that the author's decision on the superseding criterion is pending. The test is not wrong against the spec. The recorded text still needs the author's decision.

Upheld as advisory. Nothing checks AC-24's 'its other assertions unchanged' for tests/unit/module-migrations.test.ts. The script also cannot tell this item's edit from the sibling's knowledge-7 rows. The sharing row is asserted on every path the reviewer lists.
Upheld as advisory. AC-21's 'hash only for candidates with a ledger record' is proven on the helpers, and no wouldLeave test would fail if every candidate were hashed.
Upheld as advisory. 'Never the error's message' is checked only as the absence of the literal error.message. The pinned sentences still fail if the change is reverted.
Upheld as advisory. install's legacy prompt is covered only through unit tests of askYesNo, never through install.ts.
Upheld as advisory. The warning is not asserted to name WIZARDINGCODE_MEM_SHARE_AREAS. The rest of AC-12's warning is pinned.
Upheld as advisory. The memory count cannot tell the store from the copy. The no-.replaced- check at line 386 still pins the criterion.

Upheld as advisory, at the declaration's real line (the reviewer cited 523; `frontmatter: string` is at line 153). OutgoingEntry.frontmatter carries the author's name (src/modules/knowledge/author.ts), and ADR 0025's lists do not name author attribution. Nothing is sent in this part, so no personal data leaves today. Part 6 should either name the author as leaving or pin the frontmatter fields that may leave.

Lowered from defect to advisory. Question 2's premise does not hold: the branch is declared. spec.md:305 says 'the viewer's restore toast appends the same sentence' when sharingReset > 0. It is missing only from the state lists of the Sharing and Across projects pages (spec.md:279-280), which do not cover the Backups page. The cited evidence, review/ui/manifest.json, is not listed in a review/ui-evidence.json (none exists) and is not review/design-lint.json. The finding then names a diff line (diff.patch:33447) without a reason a capture cannot show it, and a capture of the Backups restore toast is possible. So the evidence rule for a ui-ux defect is not met. What remains is advisory: no capture of the toast was taken, and the copy reads '(1 projects)' for one project while the CLI's sentence uses plural() (a copy slip, not a raw error or placeholder under question 5).
Upheld as advisory. The projects line reads '1 projects share knowledge' with no singular (review/ui/settings-sharing-problems@1512.png). This is a copy slip.

Upheld as advisory. The problems alert shows the loader's lower-case strings, which name the environment variable (review/ui/settings-sharing-problems@1512.png). The spec asks for the problems joined by ' · ', and they are neither a raw error nor a path.

Upheld as advisory. The level pill sits inside the links cell instead of after it (review/ui/projects-row-pill-knowledge@1512.png). This is a placement note against the spec. AC-10's 'pill only above Nothing' holds.

Advisory, as ruled in the earlier rounds. The one console entry (review/ui/console-settings-sharing-error.json) is Chrome's network log of the 500 the session induced on purpose by making the data directory read-only. The page itself logs nothing and shows only the plain toast. The file is also not listed in a review/ui-evidence.json, so it cannot carry a ui-ux defect.

Advisory. The declared loading and saving states are under notCaptured as transient states of under a second, with their texts asserted in tests/unit/ui-sharing-copy.test.ts. The manifest has no summary.missing, and there is no review/ui-evidence.json with plan viewports. The rubric calls 'a loading state missing under a second' an advisory. The reviewer filed responsive, keyboard, axe, motion, vitals and audit as Not answerable: a gap in the run, not a finding on a line.
Lowered to advisory (debt). The existing links toast still shows error.message. This item's own sharing toasts use fixed sentences.

Upheld as advisory, as in round two. The rollback is stated, and the migration's lack of a down path has its reason. The narrower case is not named: a 0.6.0 restore of a backup taken under this release brings back that copy's levels, counter and generation with no restore row. Nothing leaves in this part, and the levels show in the viewer and in share status, so no risk defect applies. spec.md:359 and ADR 0025's rollback paragraph should name the case before parts 5 and 6 rely on the generation.
Upheld as advisory. sharingStatus calls wouldLeave unguarded, so a read error there would fail the whole status report instead of only the sharing line. The failure is visible, not silent.
Upheld as advisory. Plan step 18's 'in its own try' is not in the code. Today the check cannot throw, because loadPolicy never throws and the rest of the check is pure.
Lowered to advisory (debt). WAL is turned on only at creation, so a restored store stays in DELETE journal mode. This predates the item (probes/restore-journal-mode.md) and is its own item.
Lowered to advisory (debt). writeEnvFile treats any read failure as a new file. The code is old. This item adds callers, and the sharing lists themselves fail closed.

Upheld as advisory. policy.ts imports six read helpers from store.ts, against the Design's 'neither imports the other'. The direction is still one way and there is no cycle. Fix the Design sentence or move the helpers into a read leaf.

Upheld as advisory. The viewer writes SharingReport, SharingChange and PolicyChange again by hand and no test pins them. Importing them as types only, as Level and Root already are, would bind them.

Lowered to advisory (debt of the sibling item 2026-11-09-001). Readers outside the knowledge module guard with moduleSchemaState instead of requireSchema. This item's report.ts follows the sanctioned pattern (AC-21).

Upheld as advisory. No retention is stated for sharing_ledger or sharing_changes, and this item writes no ledger row. Part 6 must state retention before it writes the ledger.
